clue.text: Tied up and has no food

blocks.note: first meaning: held securely, unable to move
second meaning: went without eating, as in a religious observance

explanation.surface: A captive who is bound and also left without anything to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses use the past tense: held firmly in place, and observed a period of going without meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Something secured tightly was held firm, while someone abstaining from meals observed a fast; one phrase covers both.

clue.text: The old way up to the squirrel's nest

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are written from the bottom, so they read backwards

blocks.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the
Rd is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: An old route leading up a tree to where a squirrel lives.
explanation.walkthrough: YE is the old form of 'the' (as in 'Ye Olde Tea Shoppe'); YE plus RD, written upwards, gives DREY.
explanation.definitionFit: A drey is the specific name for the twiggy nest built by a squirrel in a tree.

clue.text: One looking for a radioactive isotope

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who traces or tracks things down
second meaning: a substance followed through a body or system by its radiation

explanation.surface: Someone hunting for a radioactive substance, perhaps with a Geiger counter.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface runs the two halves together as one searcher; split it after 'for'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who traces things is one, and in medicine a radioactive marker followed through the body is also called one.

clue.text: Points to raise in a republic

indicators.note: to raise something in a down entry is to lift it upward, so the following word is written bottom to top

blocks.note: east and south, two compass points
taken as written
taken as written, then turned upward
taken as written

explanation.surface: Debating points to bring up in the parliament of some republic.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'in' is raised: ES + TO + NI + A.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic state that has been an independent parliamentary republic since 1991.

clue.text: Composer has part written up for a single person

indicators.note: in a down entry, text written upward runs from bottom to top, so the word reads backwards

blocks.note: Johann Sebastian Bach, the German composer
a part in a play or film

explanation.surface: A composer has written a solo part for one performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single person' sounds like a soloist, but it means an unmarried man.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor is an unmarried man, someone single in the sense of not having a spouse.

clue.text: Narrow escape after cutting it fine?

blocks.note: first meaning: a lucky escape from danger by a tiny margin
second meaning, read literally: the result of a razor passing very near the skin

explanation.surface: Escaping disaster by a whisker after leaving things to the last moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting it fine' usually means leaving little time; the question mark invites the barber's literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a near miss, while literally a razor run very near the skin gives a smooth result.

clue.text: Rush about, madly calling

blocks.note: first meaning: to hurtle wildly and out of control
second meaning: a profession or lifelong vocation

explanation.surface: Someone dashing around wildly while shouting out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madly' looks like an anagram signal, but it belongs to the first meaning; 'calling' is a vocation, not shouting.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to move swiftly and uncontrollably; as a noun it is a person's chosen occupation or vocation.

clue.text: Carry a gun with sleeves rolled up, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the phrase is spelt differently from how it is pronounced

blocks.note: with sleeves pushed back the limbs are uncovered

explanation.surface: A gunman with rolled-up sleeves, ready for action.
explanation.walkthrough: The right to bear arms is the phrase from the US Constitution's Second Amendment.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear is to carry, and arms are weapons, so the phrase means to carry firearms.

clue.text: Keeping up an empty apartment

blocks.note: the indefinite article
empty means holding nothing, shown as the round letter that looks like zero
the British word for an apartment

explanation.surface: Paying for an unoccupied apartment while trying to stay solvent.
explanation.walkthrough: An empty flat has nothing inside, so O goes inside FLAT, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Afloat describes staying on the surface of water, or staying solvent, both forms of not sinking.

clue.text: Postpone a visit

blocks.note: first meaning: to suspend or defer, as a court does with an execution
second meaning: a period spent somewhere as a guest

explanation.surface: Putting off a trip to see someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal suspension of proceedings is one sense, and a short sojourn at a hotel or friend's house is another.

clue.text: Clipper of the line

blocks.note: surface reading: a fast sailing ship belonging to a shipping line
setter's reading: a small device clipped onto a washing line to hold laundry

explanation.surface: A sleek sailing vessel of a famous shipping company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clipper' suggests a tea clipper and 'line' a shipping line; really the line is for drying washing.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden or plastic clip that grips wet laundry to a washing line is exactly a thing that clips onto the line.

clue.text: Tropical disease?

blocks.note: surface reading: an illness found in hot equatorial countries
setter's reading: a disease whose name is also that of one of the two tropics of latitude

explanation.surface: A malady caught in the tropics.
explanation.walkthrough: One tropic, at about 23 degrees north, shares its name with a serious disease.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tropic of Cancer is the northern tropic, and the same word names a malignant disease.

clue.text: In the sphere of misdeeds this is a record

definitions.text: In the sphere of misdeeds this is a record

blocks.clueFragment: In the sphere of misdeeds this is a record
blocks.note: surface reading: an unbeaten achievement, a record for wrongdoing

blocks.clueFragment: In the sphere of misdeeds this is a record
blocks.note: setter's reading: the police document listing a person's offences

explanation.surface: Someone boasting of a record-breaking feat of misbehaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' tempts as a best-ever achievement; here it is a written log kept by the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A police charge document listing offences against a suspect is the written record of their wrongdoing.

clue.text: Your ills may turn out to be imaginary

indicators.note: things that turn out differently are rearranged, so the letters are reshuffled into a new order

blocks.note: the two words taken together as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A doctor reassuring a hypochondriac that the complaints are all in the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illusory is based on illusion, so it is not real but only imagined.

clue.text: One refusing to work in the forward line

blocks.note: first meaning: a worker taking part in industrial action
second meaning: an attacking player in football

explanation.surface: A lazy footballer who won't put in the effort up front.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is 'one' carried over: one in the forward line.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker who withdraws labour in a dispute and a football team's goalscoring attacker share the same name.

clue.text: Always increasing?

blocks.note: first meaning: for all time, forever
second meaning, split in two

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second sense needs the word split into two: ever more, steadily growing.
explanation.definitionFit: The poetic word means forever, and as two words it describes something growing continually larger.

clue.text: Divorce and go to pieces

blocks.note: first meaning: the ending of a marriage or relationship
second meaning: to shatter or fall apart

explanation.surface: Someone whose marriage ends and who then falls apart emotionally.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the noun, a split; the second is the verb, written as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A split between partners is one sense, and shattering into fragments is the physical sense of the same phrase.

clue.text: Sound simple

blocks.note: first meaning: intact, in good condition
second meaning: natural and unaffected, not corrupted by luxury

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like noise and 'simple' like easy; both actually describe something undamaged and innocent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something undamaged is in good condition, and a person or place untouched by sophistication remains natural and plain.

clue.text: It's deeply opposed to the devil

definitions.text: It's deeply opposed to the devil

blocks.clueFragment: It's deeply opposed to the devil
blocks.note: surface reading: something profoundly hostile to Satan, like a saint

blocks.clueFragment: It's deeply opposed to the devil
blocks.note: setter's reading: the other half of the idiom about a dilemma, between the devil and the deep one

explanation.surface: A force of good that is fundamentally hostile to Satan.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'between the devil and the deep blue sea' means facing two equally bad choices; 'deeply' points to the deep.
explanation.definitionFit: In the saying about a hopeless dilemma, the alternative set against the devil is the deep ocean.

clue.text: Herein a peculiar tale, out of this world

indicators.note: something peculiar is odd or out of order, so the word after it is rearranged
the word before is placed inside the reshuffled word that follows

blocks.note: split as two words: the first four letters are taken as written, and the last two are the container signal
taken as written, then reshuffled

explanation.surface: A storyteller announcing a strange, otherworldly story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herein' must be split into 'Here' and 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means heavenly or delicately unearthly, as if belonging to a realm beyond the material one.

clue.text: First of the inclinations of vagrants

indicators.note: the first of a word means only its opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of this word
ramps are slopes or inclines

explanation.surface: A first-hand account of the tendencies of homeless wanderers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclinations' suggests tendencies, but here it means physical slopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tramps are people with no fixed home who wander from place to place, the same as vagrants.

clue.text: Where the batsman stands about in case

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits within its boundaries, so the first word goes inside the second

blocks.note: re is Latin for concerning or about
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions on where a cricketer should take guard, just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is the white line marked near each wicket where the batsman takes position.
explanation.definitionFit: The crease is the painted line by the stumps behind which a cricket batsman stands to receive the ball.

clue.text: Battered fish she accepted

indicators.note: something accepted is taken in, so one word is held inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a common food fish

explanation.surface: She took delivery of a portion of fish fried in batter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battered fish' reads as fish and chips; 'Battered' is really the definition, meaning beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosh someone is to strike them with a short heavy club, so coshed means beaten or battered.

clue.text: Beyond the scope of a plumber

definitions.text: Beyond the scope of a plumber

blocks.clueFragment: Beyond the scope of a plumber
blocks.note: surface reading: a job too difficult for someone who fixes pipes

blocks.clueFragment: Beyond the scope of a plumber
blocks.note: setter's reading: too deep for anyone who plumbs, that is sounds, the depth of water

explanation.surface: A household repair too complicated for the person called in to fix the pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: To plumb is to measure depth with a weighted line; a fathom is six feet of depth.
explanation.definitionFit: Water too deep to measure by sounding has no reachable bottom, so it is unmeasurably deep.

clue.text: It's made to last

blocks.note: surface reading: something built to be durable
setter's reading: something shaped on a cobbler's last, the foot-shaped form

explanation.surface: A sturdy product built to endure.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is the wooden foot-shaped block a cobbler builds footwear around.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear is traditionally formed over a cobbler's model foot, so it is literally made on that form.

clue.text: Circus performer to making an impression

definitions.note: a verb phrase: the answer is the verb, to stamp an impression

blocks.note: first meaning: a marine mammal trained to balance balls in a circus
second meaning: to stamp a design into wax

explanation.surface: An entertainer at the circus trying hard to impress.
explanation.definitionFit: A trained aquatic mammal performs tricks in the ring, and an embossed wax stamp leaves an impression on a document.

clue.text: A new paper to be published

indicators.note: a new version of something is remade, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then reshuffled

explanation.surface: A fresh newspaper about to come off the presses.
explanation.definitionFit: When a book or article comes out in print it is said to appear, meaning it is issued to the public.

clue.text: Watch dances in which one has pupils

blocks.note: to eye is to watch closely
balls are formal dances

explanation.surface: A teacher watching dances attended by the students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupils' suggests schoolchildren; here they are the dark centres of the eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: The pupil is the opening at the centre of the iris, located in each round organ of sight.
